<reason>Both sides argued well and stayed within closed-book discipline (no fake citations; the Iceland/UK pilots and Ford were used at appropriate vagueness). PRO built a clean, memorable frame: the workweek is already legislated, the coordination trap explains non-diffusion, and productivity growth has not shown up in the clock. But PRO's route depended on the pay-protection clause being fundable, and CON attacked exactly there. CON's asymmetry — universal, certain hourly cost versus sectoral, self-selected, speculative offsets — was pressed consistently and never quantified away. CON also converted PRO's own nursing answer ("more shifts staffed by more people") into a concession that continuous-coverage sectors get the full cost with no offset, then used a pointed pressure question to extract "the public purse pays it," and weighed that persuasively as a large spending program smuggled through labor law. Crucially, CON answered PRO's strongest pressure question (name an alternative that changes the default and escapes the first-mover trap) with a concrete, responsive mechanism: universal premium pricing above 32 hours without the pay-protection decree. PRO's closing rejoinder — that this makes the worker buy her own day off — was the sharpest PRO moment and landed real damage, and the externality point ("uncosted to the firm is not costless to society") remained live but asserted rather than developed. On net, CON both blunted PRO's mechanism and supplied a cleaner comparative alternative, and turned PRO's Ford example against it (statute is needed only where the math fails, i.e., where it inflicts pure loss). CON made the decision easier.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's pressure question forcing PRO to name who pays for hospital coverage, followed by PRO's admission that "the public purse pays it," which CON reframed as a large spending program passed through labor law without a budget debate — combined with CON's turn on the Ford example (voluntary adoption where the math works; statute needed only where it fails).</best_rebuttal>
